cells.tense: You're at the table while the shape is still forming, and your hand is on it now.
cells.verb: You're giving a shape to what's ending, so what's left can be held.
cells.place: You're standing at the close of a chapter you've already accepted is closing.
cells.ask: Offer one structure looser than you'd normally trust — one full step less control than feels right — and watch what it feeds next: a knowing about what to attend to that arrives before you can argue with it.
cells.core: You're the one giving shape to what's ending, and you know it. Not hauling debris around and not pretending the chapter isn't over — you're making the close workable, so the next thing has somewhere to begin. The clearing isn't wreckage in your hands; it's architecture. Things make sense in your presence, and you can feel that they do.
cells.sheetLine: You give a shape to the ending so something can be held.

cells.tense: You're living a chapter ahead, bracing for a door that hasn't closed yet.
cells.verb: You're building a container for what's ending — and reinforcing it past the point of usefulness.
cells.place: You're standing at a transformation you keep trying to finish on your own schedule.
cells.ask: Look at the mechanism instead of its contents — one clear look at how this ending actually works, not one more plan for surviving it — and what comes back is depth that doesn't need the plan: patterns seen well enough to free you.
cells.core: You've built the frame before checking the room. The organization isn't serving the ending anymore — it's replacing it, holding everything in place so well that nothing is allowed to complete. You're managing a transformation that keeps being asked to wait for your permission, and the bracing is costing you the very ground you meant to save.
cells.sheetLine: The structure has stopped holding the ending and started preventing it.

cells.tense: You're still standing at a door you already walked through, looking for the paperwork.
cells.verb: You're trying to organize what's ending, and the pieces don't assemble.
cells.place: You're somewhere in a transformation that's been waiting for you to arrive.
cells.ask: Let one false thing fall all at once — not by effort but by seeing straight through it — and what comes back is clarity sharp enough to let what couldn't hold simply go: true insight collapsing what was only ever scaffolding.
cells.core: The ends are everywhere and the shape won't take. You know something is over, maybe several things, and you can't put them in an order that holds — the shelf falls apart before you've set the first thing on it. It isn't that you don't care. The making sense has stopped, and it stopped a while back, and you've been living without it longer than you'd say.
cells.sheetLine: The ending is real and the shape around it isn't holding.

cells.tense: Your hand has been on the shape for a while now — you're just not counting it as yours.
cells.verb: You're giving a shape to what's ending around you, and you call it just making do.
cells.place: You're standing in a clearing that other people can already see.
cells.ask: Say out loud one thing you've been holding in shape for others, and honor what it ends — let it finish rather than restarted — and what comes back is felt necessity: endings you can name as endings, renewal you can stop bracing against.
cells.core: Other people are using a structure you're holding up and you'd describe yourself as formless. The ordering is happening — in how you steady things, what you quietly decide, what no longer falls apart in your room — and you credit none of it. You're doing it the whole time and calling it nothing. Meanwhile what you organize keeps working, which is exactly why it's gone unnoticed as yours.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding it in shape. You just haven't said so.
